events.title: Knox County Schools removes Alex Haley's Roots from library shelves under Tennessee Age-Appropriate Materials Act
events.summary: Knox County Schools (KCS) in Tennessee removed Alex Haley's Roots from school library shelves in May 2026, citing Tennessee's 2022 Age-Appropriate Materials Act. The district's review committee determined a passage in the novel's 84th chapter was not "age appropriate" under state law. KCS spokesperson Carly Harrington stated the decision reflected adherence to state law rather than judgment on the book's literary or cultural value. The material remains available for classroom instruction but is no longer accessible on library shelves.
events.why_relevant: The removal of a Pulitzer Prize-winning work documenting slavery from school libraries under a state law designed to restrict access to materials based on isolated passages undermines students' access to historically significant literature and constrains educational exposure to America's past.
events.basis: KCS earlier in May pulled the novel from school shelves under Tennessee's so-called Age-Appropriate Materials Act.
